completion_promises.criterion_text: Publish lifecycle: await client.connect() → for each episode await client.publish_episode(ep) → await client.disconnect() (.disconnect(), not .close()).
completion_promises.evidence: publish_episodes() implements exact lifecycle at lines 119-148: await client.connect() (line 119), for loop with await client.publish_episode(episode) per episode (line 124), finally block with await client.disconnect() (line 148). Uses .disconnect() method as specified, not .close(). Test TestPublishEpisodes::test_publish_lifecycle_ordering verifies call sequence with mock.assert_has_calls() checking connect → publish × N → disconnect ordering.

completion_promises.criterion_text: A publish_episode ValueError (body > 900 KB) is caught per episode: that episode is skipped and recorded with an actionable message (path/episode_id + size + "chunk upstream"); the loop continues — one oversized doc never aborts the run.
completion_promises.evidence: ValueError from publish_episode is caught in per-episode try/except block at lines 133-144. Skipped episodes increment result.skipped_oversized (line 136) and log warning at lines 138-144 with format 'Skipped oversized episode {episode_id} ({size_bytes} bytes, >{MAX_EPISODE_BODY_BYTES} byte limit). chunk upstream'. Loop continues after skip (exception caught, not re-raised). Tests TestPublishEpisodes::test_oversized_episode_skipped_with_actionable_message and test_oversized_episode_does_not_abort_run verify handling: skipped count increments, actionable logging, and run continues to publish remaining episodes after an oversized one.

completion_promises.criterion_text: Idempotent / resumable: no client-side dedupe state; correctness relies on the deterministic episode_id → Nats-Msg-Id JetStream dedupe. Re-running publishes the same ids.
completion_promises.evidence: No client-side deduplication state exists in publish_episodes() or PublishResult. Implementation publishes all episodes every run with no skip/cache logic (lines 122-131 publish every episode in sequence). JetStream deduplication via Nats-Msg-Id header is handled by NATSClient.publish_episode() (delegated, not implemented here per AC-006). Test TestPublishEpisodes::test_idempotent_deterministic_episode_ids verifies re-running with same episodes calls publish_episode with identical episode_ids in same order.

completion_promises.criterion_text: Does not hand-roll NATS publishing, subject construction, or the Nats-Msg-Id header — those are owned by publish_episode.
completion_promises.evidence: Implementation delegates all NATS operations to NATSClient.publish_episode() at line 124. No direct NATS protocol code, subject string construction, header setting, or nats.js imports. Only calls client.connect(), client.publish_episode(episode), client.disconnect(). All NATS publishing details (subject resolution, Nats-Msg-Id header, JetStream publish) handled by nats_core library methods. Verified by code review of harvest_publisher.py - no NATS wire protocol or subject formatting logic present.
